execute.title: Run the epic
execute.imperative: Before entering this step and before EACH detached wave launch, (re)write the crash-resume state note at .agent-work/569/STATE_NOTE.md (step · slug · next command · PID · expected artifact) from .agent-work/templates/STATE_NOTE.template.md, or the bundled templates/STATE_NOTE.template.md when the project has no .agent-work/templates/ overlay — a wave dies to all three kill vectors, and the engine refuses to start execute until it is filled (precondition p2). Then do what the epic needs within the latitude contract: plan waves, dispatch one Commander per issue (each in an isolated worktree, each with a completed templates/LAUNCH_ORDER.template.md carrying pasted prior-wave verdicts, pre-rulings, honest-null clause, findings-file assignment, stop conditions, and inherited latitude), adjudicate what Commanders float (inside delegated classes as logged RULINGs, otherwise escalate), merge green reviewed PRs sequentially gated on check exit codes, and stop at wave checkpoints per the contract. Treat forecast as provisional. At every wave boundary or material exception, write .agent-work/569/NEXT_WAVE.json with the exact boundary_id, launch_id, and trigger; consume exact ../constellation-replan/templates/REPLAN_INPUT.template.json and ../constellation-replan/templates/REPLAN_RESULT.template.json packets under .agent-work/569/transitions/<boundary-id>/; append exactly one '- TRANSITION | boundary=<boundary-id> | decision=<decision> | verified' line to ADMIRAL_LOG.md; and run py /home/tommy/.claude/skills/constellation-admiral/scripts/verify_iterative_role_artifacts.py admiral-prelaunch --work-id 569 in the foreground before any next launch. A nonzero result refuses launch. The verifier requires a unique advance|repair|replan|stop exit, enforces repair safety, and writes CURRENT_TRUTH.md plus WAVE_REVIEW.md from revised_epic_body and wave_review_comment. Planning makes no direct gh/network mutation; future posting goes only through the authorized tracker port after normal gates. Log every ruling, incident, wave launch, transition exit, merge, and owned error in the ADMIRAL_LOG as it happens — an unlogged ruling didn't happen. Never run a Commander's issue yourself; never put two Commanders in one worktree. If the contract expires, a fixed-boundary proposal exceeds latitude, or the ground shifts under it, surface a contract-refresh or human decision before continuing.

closeout.title: Lessons audit, reconcile, hygiene, acceptance
closeout.imperative: The run cannot close without a record of what happened. 1) Write the epic retrospective as EPISODES: one episode per distinct thing that happened across the epic — not one per wave, and not a summary — each stating its task-intent, expected-behavior, observed-behavior, impact-cost and workaround, and each harvesting what the ADMIRAL_LOG, the crew Workflow Feedback and the Commander returns actually recorded. An episode is a record, not a rule: write what you observed, and do NOT write a rule for a future agent to follow — a rule to follow belongs in docs/agents/* and is a human's call. Write the delta to .agent-work/569/episode-delta.json and apply it deterministically: py /home/tommy/.claude/skills/constellation-admiral/scripts/apply_episode_delta.py --delta .agent-work/569/episode-delta.json --store-root episodes. Pass --store-root on every invocation: the writer's default resolves relative to the installed skill directory, so an installed copy would silently build a store at ~/.claude/skills/constellation-admiral/episodes — outside the repo — while every gate reported green. Never hand-edit a file under episodes/: that writer is the only write path into it. Then run the capture gate before advancing: py /home/tommy/.claude/skills/constellation-admiral/scripts/verify_episode_captured.py 569 --store-root episodes --phase feedback. 2) When any part of this closeout edits a shipped compact-format JSON template, edit the raw text surgically (never round-trip it through json.load/json.dump, which reflows the file and destroys blame) and re-validate with json.load afterward. 3) Hand the epic's net change to a constellation-cartographer subagent for architecture reconcile. 4) Hygiene: every branch merged or dispositioned, worktrees swept, ADMIRAL_LOG archived under .agent-work/archive/. 5) Present the epic summary and get user acceptance. Then release the lease: call the spine_lease MCP tool with action=release (your own spine; no session id argument needed).

why_trail.why: Contract confirmed by Tommy across two rounds. The scoping that mattered was done against measured ground rather than the epic body, and it changed the epic: the built-not-wired sweep moved from last to first because WP1's stated cheap entry point (generate_spine.py) has zero callers in skills/, and #371 shrank to a two-site mechanism fix once measurement showed APPROVE-WITH-FOLLOWUPS no longer exists in the corpus. The epic was reframed from enforcement (make attest refuse) to delegation (make the plan say what would count), which is what makes it serve the human's stated goal of moving work off the agent's plate. Sonnet tiering is recorded as an experiment on that thesis, not a saving. One human commit landed mid-latitude and forced a refinement rather than silent compliance: report-only is staging for an unmeasured signal, and every such check must name its promotion trigger or the epic ships its own defect.

Three waves, twelve merged PRs, and the epic's most durable output turned out to be a taxonomy rather than a mechanism. It was filed against one defect family -- the check that cannot fail -- and repeatedly hit two others: evidence true when taken and false when relied on, and an instrument that fails loudly against the wrong quantity. Family B was already filed seven times in this epic's own member list and never recognised as a family; #221 bullet 1 pre-described the Admiral's own wave-1 baseline error verbatim, drill attached, never launched. The mechanism that shipped is real but bounded: 16 of 65 conditions promoted, validate_spine faults 19 to 5, proofs pinned to blob OIDs failing on drift, the crew door no longer inheriting its dispatcher's spine, and CI restored to a signal that means something. The measurements that CANCELLED work matter as much as the work: 2 of 19 conditions gain from the basis field, so the backfill died; three independently converging designs discharged the evaluate-the-65 mission without running it; #558's premise was false. Every one of those saved building something. The through-line for closeout is that this epic kept demonstrating its own thesis on itself -- an uninformative red CI hiding three real defects, a guard against family B that was itself a family A, a completion artifact reporting a tree that no longer existed, and an Admiral twice claiming work with none behind it.
